# theloop

> theloop is an open-source agent loop that runs as a stateless HTTP service. One `POST /runs` is one run: the request carries the provider, model, API key, prompt, full history, tools (URL + JSON schema) and limits. The engine runs model → tools → model until a final answer, streams text over SSE, delivers the result and billing-grade usage by callback, and keeps no state between calls. Apache 2.0, Node 22, TypeScript.

Key facts:

- Status: v1.0, contract frozen (semver, no breaking changes within 1.x). Latest release: v1.2.0 (2026-10-28). The implementation is young; expect fixes, not contract changes.
- Built for teams that ship assistants to many users: multi-tenant by construction, because there is no tenant state in the engine.
- Not a framework or SDK you import. Your backend (the "harness") stores history, assistants, tools and operations, and owns approvals and billing. The engine owns the loop, streaming, cancellation, limits and accounting.
- Write tools are intents: a tool with `effect: "write"` answers `deferred` with an operation id; the mutation happens in your system after approval, never inside a tool call. A prompt-injected model can ask for an action but cannot carry it out, provided your endpoints follow the trust model.
- Usage: one record per provider attempt, including failed and interrupted ones, with uncached input, cache read/write and an explicit `estimated` flag. Optional cost from your price list; token and cost budgets.
- Delivery: at-least-once callback with retries, deduplicated by `run_id`; results readable at `GET /runs/{id}` for recovery.
- Egress: HTTPS only, host allowlist, no private IPs, no redirects, header filtering. Provider keys never appear in logs, SSE, callbacks or error bodies.
- Providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, DeepSeek, GLM (z.ai), GigaChat, MiniMax and any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with per-request keys, per-key queues and AIMD rate limiting.
- Skills and deferred tools (since v1.1.0): `skills[]` in the `SKILL.md` shape and tools with `defer_loading`. The model loads a skill's instructions and tools mid-run with the built-in `load_skill`, or finds deferred tools with the built-in `search_tools` (BM25). The engine stays stateless, and the prompt cache survives on Anthropic (`tool_reference`).
- Not in v1: MCP tools, multiple instances, history summarization, RAG, multi-agent orchestration. Several of these are proposals in the roadmap.
- Run it: `git clone https://github.com/paveler/theloop.git && cd theloop && npm install && npm run dev` (Node 22.9+), or `docker run -p 8080:8080 -e ENGINE_TOKEN=change-me -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=… ghcr.io/paveler/theloop:1`.
- Website: https://theloopengine.com · Repository: https://github.com/paveler/theloop · Docker image: ghcr.io/paveler/theloop
- Author: Pavel Ershov (https://github.com/paveler), pavel@ershov.org — questions, feedback and integrations welcome.

## Docs

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/README.md): overview, quickstart, trust model, how it fits, code map
- [SPEC v1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/SPEC.md): the contract — HTTP API, message format, tools and `effect`, result and callback, usage and billing, providers, limits, reliability, errors, deployment, harness obligations
- [sqlite-harness example](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/examples/sqlite-harness/README.md): a complete harness on SQLite — history, a read tool, a write tool with approval, continuation, recovery

## Optional

- [CHANGELOG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/CHANGELOG.md): what changed in each release and what is on main
- [RFC 0001: skills and deferred tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/docs/rfcs/0001-skills-and-deferred-tools.md): the design of `skills[]`, `defer_loading`, `load_skill` and `search_tools`
- [ROADMAP](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/ROADMAP.md): proposals — more providers, model fallbacks, MCP tools, OpenTelemetry, compaction, sub-runs, a reference harness
- [AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paveler/theloop/main/AGENTS.md): how to work on the code — commands, architecture rules, conventions, tests, releases
- [Repository](https://github.com/paveler/theloop): source, issues, releases
- [Landing page](https://theloopengine.com/): the human-friendly version of this file
- [Changelog](https://theloopengine.com/changelog/): release notes, newest first; v1.1.0 added skills, deferred tools and search_tools; v1.1.1 and v1.1.2 are fixes; v1.2.0 adds an answer on step limits, a disk journal and presentation invariants
- [Compare](https://theloopengine.com/vs/): two-minute comparisons with LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI, Vercel AI SDK, LiteLLM and n8n
- [theloop vs LangChain](https://theloopengine.com/vs/langchain/): a framework you import vs a stateless service you call
- [theloop vs LangGraph](https://theloopengine.com/vs/langgraph/): checkpointed graphs vs one run that keeps no state
- [theloop vs OpenAI](https://theloopengine.com/vs/openai/): OpenAI's hosted, stateful agent APIs vs a self-hosted stateless loop for any provider
- [theloop vs Vercel AI SDK](https://theloopengine.com/vs/ai-sdk/): a TypeScript library with an in-process loop vs the same engine behind HTTP
- [theloop vs LiteLLM](https://theloopengine.com/vs/litellm/): an AI gateway that routes model calls vs a service that runs the whole agent loop; they compose
- [theloop vs n8n](https://theloopengine.com/vs/n8n/): a visual workflow builder with AI nodes vs a headless agent engine to embed in your product
